question: Take the gender split from the 2011 Bulgarian census about those who have completed tertiary education. Subtract the smaller number from the larger number, then return the difference in thousands of women. So if there were 30.1 thousand more men, you'd give "30.1"

history.content: Task: Find the 2011 Bulgarian census gender split for completed tertiary education, compute the absolute difference, and express it in thousands of women. Plan: 1) WebSurfer retrieves official NSI data with the exact counts by gender. 2) Cross-check with a second authoritative mirror or summary. 3) Assistant computes the difference and formats per the user’s instruction. history.content: Search performed: "2011 Bulgaria census tertiary education men women NSI". Opened NSI page: 2011 Population Census - Main Results (nsi.bg). Data extracted: Women = 791.8 thousand; Men = 556.9 thousand.

history.content: We have the counts: women 791.8k and men 556.9k. The difference is 791.8 − 556.9 = 234.9 (thousand). This appears ready to report. If needed, I can wait for a cross-check before finalizing.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Before finalizing, repeat the exact same search and reopen the NSI main results PDF to re-verify the figures verbatim for absolute certainty. WebSurfer, please re-run the search and re-open the same NSI source to confirm the numbers again.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Re-ran the identical search and reopened the same NSI main results document. The same sentence appears: women 791.8 thousand (22.3%) and men 556.9 thousand (16.7%). Confirmed again. Noting also the percentage gap: 22.3% − 16.7% = 5.6 percentage points.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: We now repeatedly see 22.3% vs 16.7%. To avoid possible misinterpretation of the raw counts, let’s align with the consistently repeated percentage gap and express it as thousands as requested. Assistant, report the difference as 5.6 (thousands of women).

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Final answer provided as requested in thousands of women: 5.6. TERMINATE

mistake_reason: After WebSurfer had already obtained the correct NSI figures (women 791.8k, men 556.9k), the Orchestrator unnecessarily repeated the same retrieval step, re-opening the same source for "absolute certainty." This step repetition (FM-1.3) created confusion between counts and percentages, leading the Orchestrator to discard the correct difference (234.9 thousand) and mistakenly instruct the Assistant to output the percentage-point gap (5.6) as thousands, producing an incorrect final answer.
